body:
Measured across three independent lanes on 2026-08-21:
- test/gateway/probation-frame.test.ts: failed 2-of-4 full runs at load 26.6-42 (48 vitest
  workers from parallel lanes), "the renderer could not start" / 500-instead-of-200 on
  writeRoute; passes 6/6 in isolation; base tree also fails under the same load. Frozen by
  T35. The file boots with the default 10s renderSpawnTimeoutMs.
- test/gateway/closure-cost.test.ts: red once at load 39-42, unreproducible in isolation,
  failure message not captured. 20s testTimeout suspected, not proven.

The flaky-test rule says fix now, and the fix is NOT widening assertions: determine per file
whether it is a RAIL bug (fixture not pinning the spawn budget it depends on — probation-frame
never sets renderSpawnTimeoutMs, so it inherits a default sized for real doors, not loaded CI)
or a SPEC-ACCURACY bug. The likely fix — the fixture setting an explicit spawn budget — edits
frozen files, so it needs the two-PR rail-renames authorization. Constraint: a rename pair is
a SINGLE-LINE substitution (printable ASCII, 3-120 chars, no newlines), so the fixture change
must be expressed as same-line rewrites of existing Gateway.boot lines, never added lines; this ticket's first
deliverable is the measured case for that authorization (both probes red/green documented),
which is Myk's merge by construction. Related: the render-sandbox ULID tickets
(T-01KZW8KBMQ…, T-01KZW8KVJK…) own the renderSpawnTimeoutMs clock-naming question — read them
first and fold rather than fork.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) Both files' failure modes are reproduced under controlled load and attributed (rail vs
    spec-accuracy), with the fix named per file. Verify: the measurement transcript in the PR.
(b) The authorization PR (if frozen edits are needed) carries byte-exact pairs and both
    probes. Verify: rails-guard-ci on the pair.
(c) After the fix lands, ten consecutive full-suite runs under the same load show zero flakes
    in both files. Verify: the run transcript.

Merge tier: the authorization is Myk's (frozen rails); the mechanical rename PR follows on
its evidence.
title: Two frozen rails flake under concurrent-lane load — spawn budgets meet a loaded box
